additional_info.subject: RE: ID0455767-DC/Si-D/CZ-[MP / S5 170003652] Charging Issue CRM:03098000035
additional_info.body:
Dear support team,
Looking into the logs I spotted following.
We get maximum power limit from OCPP backend via parameter SetCharging profile at value
118472
W. SetChargingProfile value changes but it is never smaller than 80 kW throughout the transaction.
2025-10-15T07:29:21.845275+00:00 [FW080005G2] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/bf7de88a7536[794]: OCPP: Received command: SetChargingProfile (fd851915-3423-42bf-9337-321f58cd7f77) - {"connectorId":1,"csChargingProfiles":{"chargingProfileId":37035239,"stackLevel":0,"chargingProfilePurpose":"TxDefaultProfile","chargingProfileKind":"Absolute","validFrom":"2025-10-15T07:29:21Z","chargingSchedule":{"chargingRateUnit":"W","chargingSchedulePeriod":[{"startPeriod":0,"limit":
118472
,"numberPhases":3}],"startSchedule":"2025-10-15T07:29:21Z","minChargingRate":0}}}
Vehicle parameters
2025-10-15T07:29:23.130251+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  DC1: EV connected: V_Max: 825[V], I_Max:350[A], P_Max:288[kW], SoC:65[%]
After we start charging only QA21 and QA22 are on.
2025-10-15T07:29:44.194371+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  DC1: Charging Phase "P04_PRE_CHARGE" --> "P05_START_CHARGE"
2025-10-15T07:29:44.212012+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [SCO]  OGC[0]: DC1-DC1_QA21-22, COMMAND: on, FEEDBACK: on, BLOCKING: yes, OPRSTATE: Normal(all ok), CHRGOPRMODE: 6, CTRL_DC_UNIT: DC1
2025-10-15T07:29:44.597701+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  DC1: Charging Phase "P05_START_CHARGE" --> "P06_CHARGE"
And that does not change even when we reach 80 kW and car is requesting higher power (is able to charge with higher power at this SoC).
2025-10-15T07:30:27.625503+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  |ID=281|DC1: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=
80
|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=106|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=
80
|EVSE_NowCur[A]=106|EVSE_NowVol[V]=757.2|EV_TarCur[A]=106.6|EV_TarVol[V]=825|EV_SOC[%]=66|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=118|Cable_Max[A]=500|Phase=6
At that time, the most recent OCPP command specified a power limit of 118472 watts
.
Therefore, the cause of the observed 80 kW limitation must originate from another source.
2025-10-15T07:29:21.845275+00:00 [FW080005G2] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/bf7de88a7536[794]: OCPP: Received command: SetChargingProfile (fd851915-3423-42bf-9337-321f58cd7f77) - {"connectorId":1,"csChargingProfiles":{"chargingProfileId":37035239,"stackLevel":0,"chargingProfilePurpose":"TxDefaultProfile","chargingProfileKind":"Absolute","validFrom":"2025-10-15T07:29:21Z","chargingSchedule":{"chargingRateUnit":"W","chargingSchedulePeriod":[{"startPeriod":0,"limit":
118472
,"numberPhases":3}],"startSchedule":"2025-10-15T07:29:21Z","minChargingRate":0}}}
2nd case. Working accordingly.I checked the other charging session on 400V architecture. There we connect another converter group once the limit of one charger group is reached. Please see example
Parameter discovery
2025-10-15T08:13:06.051431+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  DC1: EV connected: V_Max: 408[V], I_Max:500[A], P_Max:204[kW], SoC:57[%]
Start charge with DC1-DC1_QA21-22, COMMAND: on, FEEDBACK: on, BLOCKING: yes, OPRSTATE: Normal(all ok)
2025-10-15T08:13:24.435882+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  |ID=282|DC1: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=80|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=44|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=3.5|EVSE_NowCur[A]=10|EVSE_NowVol[V]=365.9|EV_TarCur[A]=16.8|EV_TarVol[V]=408|EV_SOC[%]=55|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=204|Cable_Max[A]=500|Phase=6
But after we reach certain power QA09-10 turns on and EVSE_MaxPwr[kW] reaches higher value 204 kW
2025-10-15T08:13:32.468216+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  |ID=282|DC1: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=
80
|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=198|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=
60.5
|EVSE_NowCur[A]=161|EVSE_NowVol[V]=376.2|EV_TarCur[A]=169.7|EV_TarVol[V]=408|EV_SOC[%]=55|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=204|Cable_Max[A]=500|Phase=6
2025-10-15T08:13:32.784343+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [SCO]  SMC[0]: MG1-MG2_QA09-10, COMMAND: on, FEEDBACK: off, BLOCKING: no, OPRSTATE: Normal(all ok), CHRGOPRMODE: 6, CTRL_DC_UNIT: DC1
2025-10-15T08:13:32.971595+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  |ID=282|DC1: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=
204
|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=198|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=63.1|EVSE_NowCur[A]=168|EVSE_NowVol[V]=376.2|EV_TarCur[A]=179.2|EV_TarVol[V]=408|EV_SOC[%]=55|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=204|Cable_Max[A]=500|Phase=6
Then the power changes from OCPP command to
153027
watts.
2025-10-15T08:17:07.199412+00:00 [FW080005G2] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/bf7de88a7536[794]: OCPP: Received command: SetChargingProfile (ed35ad6d-27f5-468d-a3de-4bdab640716f) - {"connectorId":1,"csChargingProfiles":{"chargingProfileId":37036924,"stackLevel":0,"chargingProfilePurpose":"TxProfile","chargingProfileKind":"Absolute","validFrom":"2025-10-15T08:17:06Z","chargingSchedule":{"chargingRateUnit":"W","chargingSchedulePeriod":[{"startPeriod":0,"limit":
153027
,"numberPhases":3}],"startSchedule":"2025-10-15T08:17:06Z","minChargingRate":0},"transactionId":5726328}}
2025-10-15T08:17:07.244072+00:00 [FW080005G2] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [DCC]  |ID=282|DC1: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=153|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=286|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=99.1|EVSE_NowCur[A]=253|EVSE_NowVol[V]=391.2|EV_TarCur[A]=251.7|EV_TarVol[V]=408|EV_SOC[%]=63|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=199|Cable_Max[A]=500|Phase=6
Thank you for your reaction.
Kind regards,
Milan

additional_info.subject: 0455767 - ID0455767-DC/Si-D/CZ-[MP / S5 170003652] Charging Issue CRM:00472000425
additional_info.body:
Hello Milan,
The power is limited to the primary DC group available power because when addressing the second DC group, it fails on the Precharge voltage check.
We don't know why is this happening, I have opened an R&D ticket to investigate the root cause.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso

additional_info.subject: RE: 0455767 - ID0455767-DC/Si-D/CZ-[MP / S5 170003652] Charging Issue CRM:00472000425
additional_info.body:
Hello Milan,
Thank you for reporting this issue.
I wanted to provide you with an update: the topic you raised is currently being processed by R&D. While they are actively working on a resolution, we do not yet have a confirmed timeline for when the fix will be available or implemented.
Details regarding the fix will be shared in a future release note, rather than in the immediate next firmware versions.
Since there are no further actions pending from the service side at this time, I will proceed with closing this ticket.
We truly appreciate you bringing this problem to our attention.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso
Siemens S.A.

2845-547 Corroios, Portugal

additional_info.subject: RE: 0455767 - ID0455767-DC/Si-D/CZ-[MP / S5 170003652] Charging Issue CRM:00472000425
additional_info.body:
Hello Francisco,
Thank you for the reply.
When should we expect release notes regarding the slow power ramp-up?
I found out that this delay does not seem to happen on 400V architecture. See transaction ID
5746211
in
20251104_delXft-logs_gradualRampUp400V
.
On the other side, in transaction with ID
5746211
20251016_delXft-logs_slowRampUp800V
power ramp up does not react on time to the requested EV power. Compared to the 400V architecture session, there is a significant delay before a new converter group is added to the total power.
Thank you for the update.
Kind regards,
Milan
